long_biography.plain_text:
Apartment buildings with empty units and years of deferred maintenance are central to Tim Gillean’s work at Cross Equities. The firm buys neglected properties, carries out substantial improvements and markets the renovated homes to rebuild occupancy. As a founding partner, Gillean brings together equity investors, mortgage brokers and lenders, drawing on experience in acquisitions, financing and property sales.

A refinancing of three Dallas-area communities in 2020 illustrates the business model. After improvements at Spanish Villas, Spanish Rose and Spanish Ridge, the properties secured long-term Fannie Mae loans through Hunt Real Estate Capital. The financing lowered borrowing costs and released money for further apartment investments.

Flickr, Vimeo, Trip Advisor and Zillow searches found no appropriate verified personal resource. His property ownership does not by itself establish a consumer real-estate agent profile. Corporate websites are labelled separately from personal accounts.

The minimum active tag set captures the redevelopment occupation and the firm's distinct troubled-asset investment mandate. Modern supercar ownership does not establish the Classic-car collector contract. The additional cryptocurrency venture's relative importance and duration are insufficiently clear for a defining tag. No generic philanthropy or family-office tag is assigned.

The long profile's example comes from the full original lender announcement on PR Newswire, accessed after the mirrored Lument page failed retrieval. The transaction is durable career evidence; figures, exact rates and present property ownership are deliberately absent.
